Figure 5 shows the coating of AFL and GDC on Mylar substrate via a pilot scale slot-die coater. The dry coatings showed identical color and morphology to those tape cast by Redox. Different coating parameters, including the line speed, pump speed and temperature profiles for drying the coated layers, were investigated and coating quality was evaluated. Figure 5. Coating of AFL and GDC via slot-die. Figure 6 shows the wet coating of AFL on a Mylar film at different coating speeds. The coatings were defect-free and high quality at line speed below 4 FPM. Table 1 lists the coating conditions. While increasing coating speed generates thinner coating, it is critical to pay attention to the coating quality. When coating thickness is too low, defects such as uncoated regions may appear. As shown in Figure 6, uniform and defect-free coating (A & B) are produced below 4 FPM. At 4 FPM, some minor line defects on the edges would intermittently appear throughout the coating.
